name: dsh-professor-pane
description: The right pane of the DeepSeek Harness as the professor's visualization pane: course outline, class progress, the inbox, and the resolved preferences, switched by a button bar.

comments.client: `lib/client.js` is BUILT from `client/*.js` by `client/build.mjs` (`npm run build`) and committed, because dsh serves that one file from disk: `exports["./client"]` at /plugins/<id>/client.js, and nothing else under that prefix. The output is the module-loader registration form (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`) every shipped client half in node_modules/@deepseek-ai has. The build is a join, not a bundler: the modules share one factory scope and need nothing from npm, so it drops their import/export lines, concatenates them in order and wraps them. test/client-build.test.mjs fails when the built file is out of step.
comments.inject: `dsh.client.inject` names PACKAGES whose client halves must be live first, not services. ui-layout because the `details` seat is declared inside its AppFrame children table and does not exist until that entry mounts; ui-conversation because the header-action seat this pane's opener sits in is declared by its session header; client-runtime for `slots` and `sessions`. The service names this plugin injects are the `inject` export in index.js and client/pane.js.
comments.dependency: This reads the course model through `@ainar/core/src/**` — the package in ainar-node/, imported as TypeScript because Node strips types on import. Until 2026-09-16 it read `dsh-ainar-course-model/server/**`, a second compiled copy of the same model; the pane and the course-model plugin now import the one source, so a change to the model reaches both without anyone keeping two trees in step. `@ainar/core` is a dependency of the PROJECT rather than of this package, for the reason the course model's package.json gives: pnpm cannot resolve a file: spec whose absolute path contains a space, and this checkout lives under a home directory that has one. Node resolution finds it from the dsh installation's node_modules either way.
